q: How many countries share a land border with Germany?
fact: No country lying wholly within Europe has more land neighbors. They run from Denmark in the north to Switzerland and Austria in the south.

q: In what year did Karl Benz patent his three-wheeled Motorwagen, often called the first true car?
fact: In 1888 his wife Bertha drove it about 100 km on the first long car trip in history, buying fuel at a pharmacy along the way.

q: How many cantons make up Switzerland?
fact: Each canton has its own constitution, parliament and government. The newest, Jura, was created in 1979.

q: How many national languages does Switzerland have?
fact: They are German, French, Italian and Romansh. Romansh is the main language of fewer than one in a hundred Swiss.

q: In what year did Tim Berners-Lee first propose the World Wide Web while working at CERN near Geneva?
fact: The first website went public in 1991. CERN has since restored it, so it can still be visited today.

q: About how tall is the Eiffel Tower in Paris, in meters, including its antennas?
fact: Its iron expands in the summer heat, so the tower can grow by up to 15 cm on a hot day.

q: In what year was the first Tour de France cycling race held?
fact: The first race had only six stages, but some were so long that riders pedaled right through the night.

q: What is the highest number of stars the Michelin Guide, started by a French tire company, awards a restaurant?
fact: The first guide appeared in 1900 to get people driving - and wearing out tires. Three stars mean cooking 'worth a special journey'.

q: About how tall is the Leaning Tower of Pisa, in meters?
fact: It began to lean while still being built, and construction stretched over almost 200 years, from 1173 to 1372.

q: Wheels of Parmigiano Reggiano cheese must age for at least how many months?
fact: Each wheel weighs around 40 kg, and many are aged for two years or more before they are sold.

q: How many spires is Barcelona's Sagrada Familia designed to have when it is finished?
fact: Work began in 1882. Its central tower of Jesus Christ is designed to reach 172.5 m, taller than any other church in the world.

q: How many grapes do people in Spain traditionally eat at midnight on New Year's Eve?
fact: One grape goes down on each stroke of the clock, to bring luck for each month of the coming year.

q: In what year is La Tomatina, the tomato-throwing festival in Bunol, Spain, traditionally said to have first been held?
fact: Legend says it began with a scuffle at a parade. Since 2013 the festival has been ticketed, with room for about 20,000 people.

q: How many countries share a land border with Portugal, shown here?
fact: Its only land neighbor is Spain. The border between them has barely changed since 1297, making it one of the oldest in Europe.

q: In what year did the London Underground, the world's first underground railway, open?
fact: The first trains were pulled by steam engines. Londoners have long called the network 'the Tube'.

q: A Scottish Great Highland bagpipe has how many drones, the pipes that each play one steady note?
fact: Two tenor drones and one bass drone hum together, while the player fingers the melody on a separate pipe called the chanter.

q: About what percentage of the Netherlands lies below sea level?
fact: The lowest point, in a polder near Rotterdam, is almost 7 meters below sea level. Dikes, dunes and pumps keep the water out.

q: How many official languages does Belgium have?
fact: Dutch, French and German. The German-speaking community, in the east near the border, has fewer than 100,000 people.

q: In what year did Norway end its union with Sweden and become fully independent?
fact: Norwegians voted for the split, and a Danish prince was invited to become their king as Haakon VII.

q: In what year did Finland declare its independence?
fact: Independence Day falls on December 6, when many Finns light two candles in their windows.

q: Roughly how many people live in Iceland?
fact: About two thirds of them live in and around the capital, Reykjavik, leaving much of the island almost empty.

q: How many blue and white stripes run across the flag of Greece?
fact: Five stripes are blue and four are white. Blue and white are often said to recall the sea and sky of Greece.

q: On Christmas Eve, families in Poland traditionally serve how many meatless dishes?
fact: Many families also set an extra place at the table, in case an unexpected guest knocks at the door.

q: In what year did Alexey Pajitnov create the video game Tetris in Moscow?
fact: The name mixes 'tetromino', a shape made of four squares, with tennis, his favorite sport.

q: How many time zones does Russia span, from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific?
fact: When it is 8 in the morning in Kaliningrad, it is already 6 in the evening in Kamchatka.

q: In what year did Yuri Gagarin become the first person to travel into space?
fact: His flight on April 12 lasted 108 minutes and took him once around the Earth.

q: In what year was Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, launched into orbit?
fact: It was a metal ball about the size of a beach ball, and radio fans around the world could hear its beeps for three weeks.

q: In what year did Czechoslovakia peacefully split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia?
fact: The 'Velvet Divorce' took effect on January 1 without a single shot fired, and the two countries remain close friends.

q: The white peaks on Slovenia's flag show Triglav, its highest mountain. About how high is it, in meters?
fact: Slovenes like to say you only become a true Slovene once you have climbed to its summit.

q: In what year did the Channel Tunnel between England and France open?
fact: It is about 50 km long, and nearly 38 km of it runs under the sea - the longest undersea stretch of any tunnel.

q: About how long is the Danube River, in km?
fact: It rises in Germany's Black Forest and flows past four capitals - Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade - to the Black Sea.

q: How many countries are members of the European Union?
fact: The newest member is Croatia, which joined in 2013. The United Kingdom left in 2020.

q: How many European Union countries use the euro as their currency?
fact: Bulgaria became the newest member of the euro area on January 1, 2026.

q: About how high is Mont Blanc, the highest mountain in the Alps, in meters?
fact: A survey in September 2026 put it at 4,807.47 m. Its summit is a thick cap of ice and snow, so the height changes by a meter or two between surveys.

q: How many countries share a land border with China?
fact: China ties with Russia for the most neighbors of any country, from North Korea in the east to Afghanistan in the west.

q: How many yellow stars are on the flag of China?
fact: One large star is partly circled by four smaller ones, each pointing toward the center of the big star.

q: Chinese New Year celebrations traditionally last how many days, ending with the Lantern Festival?
fact: Families clean their homes before the holiday to sweep away bad luck, and children receive money in red envelopes.

q: How many animals make up the Chinese zodiac, also used in Vietnam, Korea and Japan?
fact: Each year belongs to one animal in turn. Legend says the clever rat came first by riding on the ox's back in a great race.

q: China's Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge is the world's longest bridge. About how long is it, in km?
fact: It carries the high-speed railway between Beijing and Shanghai and was finished in 2011.

q: How many prefectures is Japan divided into?
fact: The largest is Hokkaido in the far north. The smallest by area is Kagawa, famous for its udon noodles.

q: About how high is Mount Fuji, Japan's highest mountain, in meters?
fact: Fuji is an active volcano that last erupted in 1707. Hundreds of thousands of people climb it every summer.

q: Tokyo Skytree is the world's tallest tower. About how tall is it, in meters?
fact: The height was chosen on purpose: the digits 6-3-4 can be read as 'Musashi', the old name of the Tokyo region.

q: How many strings does a standard Japanese koto have?
fact: The koto is played lying on the floor. Each string rests on its own movable bridge, which the player slides to tune it.

q: In what year did Sony of Japan launch the Walkman, the first popular pocket cassette player?
fact: It let people carry their music anywhere for the first time, and the word Walkman entered dictionaries around the world.

q: In what year did India become independent?
fact: Independence Day is August 15. The prime minister raises the flag at the Red Fort in Delhi every year.

q: How many spokes does the blue wheel on the flag of India have?
fact: The wheel is the Ashoka Chakra, taken from a pillar built by Emperor Ashoka more than 2,200 years ago.

q: In standard kabaddi, the tag sport of South Asia played at the Asian Games, how many players does each team have on court?
fact: Kabaddi has been played in South Asia for thousands of years and is the national sport of Bangladesh. A pro league in India draws huge TV audiences.

q: About how high is Mount Everest, the highest mountain on Earth, in meters?
fact: The figure comes from a joint survey by China and Nepal in 2020. The mountain still rises by a few millimeters a year.

q: In what year did Sukarno and Hatta proclaim the independence of Indonesia?
fact: The proclamation was read on August 17, which is still celebrated every year with flag ceremonies and games.

q: Roughly how many islands make up the Philippines?
fact: For decades the official figure was 7,107, until a new survey with modern mapping found hundreds more.

q: How many rays does the golden sun on the flag of the Philippines have?
fact: The rays stand for the first eight provinces that rose up against Spanish rule. The three stars stand for Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao.

q: How many red and white stripes are on the flag of Malaysia?
fact: They stand for the 13 states and the federal government. The yellow star has the same number of points.

q: About how tall are the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur, in meters?
fact: From 1998 to 2004 they were the tallest buildings in the world, and they are still the tallest twin towers.

q: In a standard match of sepak takraw, the 'kick volleyball' of Southeast Asia, how many players does each team have on court?
fact: Players may not use their hands, so they kick, knee and head a woven ball over the net. A rarer 'quadrant' version uses four players a side.

q: In what year did Singapore become an independent country?
fact: Singapore left Malaysia on August 9. In the decades since, the small island has grown into one of the world's richest countries.

q: How many white stars are on the flag of Uzbekistan?
fact: The stars are usually linked to the twelve months of the year. Blue, white and green stand for sky, peace and nature.

q: How many white points form the zigzag edge on the flag of Bahrain?
fact: The five points stand for the Five Pillars of Islam. Neighboring Qatar's flag has a similar zigzag with more points.

q: How many towers of the temple of Angkor Wat appear on the flag of Cambodia?
fact: The real temple has five towers, arranged like the peaks of Mount Meru, the home of the gods in Hindu belief.

q: How many countries share a land border with Mongolia, shown here?
fact: Mongolia lies between Russia and China. It is the most thinly populated country in the world.

q: About how high is Mount Kenya, the highest mountain in Kenya, in meters?
fact: The country takes its name from the mountain, which stands just south of the Equator yet still has small glaciers.

q: In what year did Kenya become independent?
fact: Kenyans celebrate December 12 as Jamhuri Day, the 'Republic Day' in Swahili.

q: In what year did Nigeria become independent?
fact: So many African countries became independent that year - 17 in all - that it is remembered as the 'Year of Africa'.

q: In what year did Ghana become independent?
fact: Ghana was one of the first African colonies to win independence, and the black star on its flag became a symbol of African freedom.

q: How many official languages does South Africa have?
fact: South African Sign Language became the newest official language in 2023, joining English, Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans and seven others.

q: How many different colors are used on the flag of South Africa?
fact: The flag was designed in just a few weeks. Its Y shape stands for different paths coming together and moving forward as one.

q: About how high is Toubkal in Morocco, the highest peak in North Africa, in meters?
fact: It rises in the High Atlas mountains, and climbers can reach the top in two days from a village near Marrakesh.

q: In a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony, guests are usually served how many rounds of coffee?
fact: The rounds are called abol, tona and baraka. The last one is said to bring a blessing.

q: How many yellow stars form the ring on the flag of Cabo Verde?
fact: The blue of the flag stands for the Atlantic Ocean that surrounds the islands, and the white and red stripe for the road ahead.

q: How many colored bands fan out across the flag of Seychelles?
fact: The bands spread out from the lower corner by the pole, a design meant to show a young country moving into the future.

q: How many horizontal stripes does the flag of Uganda have?
fact: Black, yellow and red each appear twice. In the center stands a grey crowned crane, the national bird.

q: Victoria Falls is the largest single sheet of falling water on Earth. About how wide is it, in meters?
fact: The water plunges about 108 meters into a narrow gorge, roughly twice the height of Niagara Falls.

q: How many great pyramids stand on the Giza plateau, not counting the small queens' pyramids?
fact: They were built for three kings - Khufu, his son Khafre and Menkaure - and are guarded by the Great Sphinx.

q: South Africa's Comrades Marathon is the world's oldest ultramarathon. Roughly how long is it, in km?
fact: First run in 1921, it usually alternates between Durban and Pietermaritzburg - uphill one year, downhill the next - so its length varies a little.

q: How many African countries are landlocked, with no coast at all?
fact: By most counts that is more than on any other continent. Lesotho is unusual even among them: it is completely surrounded by South Africa.

q: How many strings does the kora, the harp-lute of West Africa, traditionally have?
fact: Its body is a large gourd covered with cowhide. Griots, the storytellers of West Africa, have played it for centuries.

q: How many red and white stripes does the flag of the United States have?
fact: There are seven red and six white stripes, one for each of the 13 colonies that declared independence.

q: In what year did the US flag first fly with 50 stars?
fact: The new star was for Hawaii. The design is usually credited to Robert Heft, who made it as a high school class project.

q: In what year was the Declaration of Independence of the United States signed?
fact: It was adopted on July 4, now the country's national holiday, celebrated with parades and fireworks.

q: How many members sit in the United States Senate?
fact: Every state sends two senators, whether it is huge California or tiny Wyoming.

q: What is the hottest air temperature ever officially recorded on Earth, measured in Death Valley, USA, in degrees Celsius?
fact: It was measured at Furnace Creek on July 10, 1913. Some experts doubt the reading, but the World Meteorological Organization still lists it as the record.

q: In what year did the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco open?
fact: Its famous color is called 'International Orange'. It was chosen so the bridge would stand out in the fog.

q: In what year did astronauts first walk on the Moon?
fact: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin of Apollo 11 stepped onto the Moon on July 20. Their footprints are still there.

q: In what year did the Wright brothers make the first powered airplane flight?
fact: The first flight, at Kitty Hawk in North Carolina, lasted just 12 seconds and covered 37 meters.

q: In what year did Alexander Graham Bell patent the telephone in the United States?
fact: Bell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland. His first words on the phone were to his assistant: 'Mr. Watson, come here.'

q: How many players does a baseball team have on the field while defending?
fact: A game normally lasts nine innings too. Baseball is also hugely popular in Japan, Cuba and the Dominican Republic.

q: In what year is the first Thanksgiving feast traditionally said to have taken place in Plymouth?
fact: The English settlers and the Wampanoag people shared the harvest feast for three days. Today it is a holiday on the fourth Thursday of November.

q: How many provinces does Canada have?
fact: Canada also has three territories in the far north: Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut.

q: How many points does the red maple leaf on the flag of Canada have?
fact: The flag was adopted in 1965. The leaf was kept simple so that it would not blur when the flag flaps in the wind.

q: Roughly how many liters of maple sap must be boiled down to make one liter of maple syrup?
fact: Sap flows in early spring, when frosty nights are followed by mild days. Canada makes most of the world's maple syrup.

q: In what year did a restaurant owner in Ontario, Canada, invent the pineapple-topped Hawaiian pizza?
fact: Sam Panopoulos, who was born in Greece, added canned pineapple to see what would happen. The pizza has nothing to do with Hawaii.

q: About how tall is Toronto's CN Tower, in meters?
fact: It was the world's tallest free-standing structure for over 30 years. Visitors can walk around its outer edge on a harness.

q: Counting the top platform as one, how many steps does the El Castillo pyramid at Chichen Itza have?
fact: The total matches the days of the year. At the equinoxes, the sunlight makes a shadow serpent seem to slide down its north stairway.

q: How many countries share a land border with Brazil?
fact: Brazil borders every country in South America except Chile and Ecuador. It also borders France, through French Guiana.

q: In what year was Brasilia inaugurated as the new capital of Brazil?
fact: Built in less than four years, the city was planned in the shape of an airplane, with buildings by architect Oscar Niemeyer.

q: In what year did Brazil declare its independence from Portugal?
fact: Prince Pedro declared it on September 7 beside a stream in Sao Paulo and was crowned as Brazil's first emperor.

q: About how tall is the statue of Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro, in meters, not counting its pedestal?
fact: Its outstretched arms span about 28 meters. It was completed in 1931 on top of Corcovado mountain.

q: How many white and blue stripes does the flag of Uruguay have?
fact: They stand for the original departments of the country. The golden Sun of May in the corner is shared with Argentina's flag.

q: How many white stars arc across the flag of Venezuela?
fact: Seven stars recalled the provinces that signed the independence declaration of 1811. The eighth was added in 2006.

q: About how high above sea level does Machu Picchu in Peru stand, in meters?
fact: The Inca city was built in the 1400s on a ridge between two peaks, and was never found by the Spanish conquerors.

q: Lake Titicaca lies high in the Andes. At about what altitude is its surface, in meters?
fact: It is often called the highest navigable lake in the world. The Uros people live on floating islands woven from reeds.

q: At about what altitude does Quito, the capital of Ecuador, stand, in meters?
fact: In 1978 its old town was one of the first two cities, with Krakow, put on UNESCO's World Heritage list.

q: In what year did Jamaica become independent?
fact: Jamaica became independent on August 6. Trinidad and Tobago followed just a few weeks later, on August 31.

q: How many green stars circle the parrot on the flag of Dominica?
fact: There is one star for each of the island's parishes. The bird is the sisserou parrot, found nowhere else on Earth.

q: How many independent countries are there in South America?
fact: French Guiana is not counted - it is part of France. Brazil alone covers almost half of the continent.

q: How many Great Lakes are there on the border of Canada and the United States?
fact: They are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario. Lake Superior alone holds enough water to cover North and South America about 30 cm deep.

q: How many states make up Australia?
fact: Australia also has two mainland territories: the Northern Territory and the Australian Capital Territory around Canberra.

q: How many white stars are on the flag of Australia?
fact: Five form the Southern Cross. The big seven-pointed Commonwealth Star stands for the states and territories joining together.

q: About how high is Mount Kosciuszko, the highest peak on mainland Australia, in meters?
fact: It was named after Tadeusz Kosciuszko, a Polish hero, by a Polish explorer. An easy walking track leads all the way to the top.

q: In what year did six British colonies unite to form the Commonwealth of Australia?
fact: Federation took effect on January 1. The colonies became the six states that still exist today.

q: In what year did the Sydney Opera House open?
fact: It was designed by Danish architect Jorn Utzon, whose sail-shaped roofs took years to work out. It joined UNESCO's list in 2007.

q: In Australian rules football, how many players does each team have on the field?
fact: The game is played on a huge oval field. Kicking the ball between the two tall middle posts scores a six-point goal.

q: In what year did Melbourne host the first Olympic Games in the Southern Hemisphere?
fact: Strict quarantine rules kept foreign horses out of Australia, so the riding events were held in Stockholm, Sweden.

q: About how high is Aoraki / Mount Cook, the highest mountain in New Zealand, in meters?
fact: A huge rock avalanche in 1991 knocked about 10 meters off its summit. Edmund Hillary trained on its slopes before climbing Everest.

q: How many red stars are on the flag of New Zealand?
fact: The stars show the Southern Cross. Unlike on Australia's flag, they are red with white borders, and the small fifth star is left out.

q: How many players does each team field in a game of rugby union?
fact: Rugby league uses 13 players and rugby sevens only 7. New Zealand's All Blacks have won the Rugby World Cup three times.

q: Roughly how many islands make up Fiji?
fact: Only about a third of them are inhabited. Most Fijians live on the two largest islands, Viti Levu and Vanua Levu.

q: How many yellow stars are on the flag of Tuvalu?
fact: The stars are laid out like a map, each one in the position of an island of the country.

q: How many points does the white star on the flag of Nauru have?
fact: The points stand for the island's 12 original tribes. The star sits just below a yellow line - the Equator - showing where Nauru lies.

q: How many independent countries are there in Oceania?
fact: Australia is by far the largest, and Papua New Guinea the second. The smallest is tiny Nauru.

q: About how deep is the deepest point of the Mariana Trench in the Pacific, in meters?
fact: If Mount Everest were set down in it, its peak would still be more than 2 km under water. Two men first reached the bottom in 1960.

q: About how far away is the Moon from the Earth on average, in km?
fact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from us, by about 3.8 cm a year - roughly as fast as fingernails grow.

q: Roughly how far is the Earth from the Sun on average, in km?
fact: Sunlight needs a little over eight minutes to cover that distance. Astronomers call it one astronomical unit.

q: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is covered by water?
fact: Almost all of it is salty ocean. Only a few percent of all the water on Earth is fresh, and most of that is frozen in ice.

q: What is the coldest air temperature ever recorded on Earth, at Vostok Station in Antarctica, in degrees Celsius?
fact: It was measured on July 21, 1983, in the middle of the dark Antarctic winter, at a research station high on the ice sheet.

q: How long is a marathon race, in km?
fact: The odd distance comes from the 1908 London Olympics, where the course was set to start at Windsor Castle and end in front of the royal box.

q: How many players does a soccer team have on the field at the start of a match?
fact: One of the eleven is the goalkeeper, the only player allowed to handle the ball, and only inside the penalty area.

q: How many rings make up the symbol of the Olympic Games?
fact: Pierre de Coubertin designed it in 1913. Together with the white background, the colors could form every national flag of that time.

q: In what year did the Gregorian calendar, used in most of the world today, first come into use?
fact: To fix the drift of the old calendar, ten days were skipped: Thursday, October 4 was followed by Friday, October 15.

q: In what year was the United Nations founded?
fact: Its charter came into force on October 24, now celebrated as UN Day. There were 51 founding members.

q: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in tennis each year?
fact: They are the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open. Winning all four in one year is called a calendar Grand Slam.

q: How many continents are there, in the model most English-speaking schools teach?
fact: They are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America. Some countries teach five or six instead.

q: How many independent countries make up Central America?
fact: From north to south: Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama.

q: Not counting its tributaries, the Amazon River flows through or along the border of how many countries?
fact: It rises in the Andes of Peru, forms a short stretch of Colombia's border and then crosses Brazil to the Atlantic. Its basin stretches into several more countries.

q: Through how many countries in South America does the Equator pass?
fact: It crosses Ecuador, which is named after it, then Colombia and Brazil, reaching the Atlantic near the mouth of the Amazon.

q: How many countries make up the Nordic countries?
fact: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden. Their flags all carry the same sideways Nordic cross.

q: How many countries are known as the Baltic states?
fact: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Estonian is related to Finnish, while Latvian and Lithuanian are cousins of each other.

q: How many countries have a coastline on the Black Sea?
fact: Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia. Deep down its water has almost no oxygen, which preserves ancient shipwrecks.

q: How many official languages does the European Union have?
fact: Every law is published in all of them, from English and German to Maltese and Irish. Irish was the last to become a full working language, in 2022.

q: The Mekong River flows through or along the border of how many countries?
fact: It runs from the Tibetan Plateau in China, along the borders of Myanmar and Thailand, through Laos and Cambodia to its delta in Vietnam.

q: How many former Soviet republics have names ending in '-stan'?
fact: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan, all in Central Asia. The ending comes from Persian and means 'land of'.

q: Asia is the largest continent. Roughly what percentage of Earth's land does it cover?
fact: Asia is also home to about six in ten of all the people on Earth.

q: How many African countries have a coastline on the Mediterranean Sea?
fact: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt. Only 14 km of water separate Morocco from Spain at the Strait of Gibraltar.

q: Africa is the second-largest continent. Roughly what percentage of Earth's land does it cover?
fact: Africa is so big that the United States, China, India and much of Europe could all fit inside it at once.

q: Into how many great island regions are the Pacific Islands usually divided?
fact: Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia. The names mean 'black islands', 'small islands' and 'many islands' in Greek.

q: How many countries share the island of New Guinea?
fact: Papua New Guinea holds the eastern half and Indonesia the western half. New Guinea is the second-largest island in the world.

q: About what percentage of all the ice on Earth lies in Antarctica?
fact: In places the ice sheet is more than 4 km thick. If it all melted, sea levels would rise by about 58 meters.

q: How many main islands make up New Zealand?
fact: The North Island and the South Island are separated by Cook Strait. The third-largest, Stewart Island, lies far to the south.

q: How many states make up the United States?
fact: The last two to join, Alaska and Hawaii, both became states in 1959. Washington, DC, is not part of any state.

q: About how tall was the Great Pyramid of Giza when it was finished, in meters?
fact: It has lost its smooth outer casing and top stones, so today it is about 138 m tall.

q: In what year did Nelson Mandela become president of South Africa?
fact: He was the country's first president elected by all its people. South Africans now mark his birthday, July 18, as Mandela Day.

q: In what year did Morocco regain its independence?
fact: Morocco is one of the oldest kingdoms in the world, and its royal family has ruled since the 1600s.

q: How many green and yellow stripes run across the flag of Togo?
fact: The stripes stand for the regions of the country. The white star in the red corner stands for hope.

q: How many red stars sit in the white disc on the flag of Burundi?
fact: The three stars stand for the national motto: Unity, Work, Progress.
